hero.title: Your heart has a story. Understand the signals.
hero.description: CardioScan helps students, researchers, and individuals explore how standard cardiovascular measurements, like blood pressure, cholesterol, and exercise stress readings, interact. Enter numbers from an existing medical report or test with sample profiles to examine how machine-learning models estimate statistical risk patterns for educational exploration.
hero.what_you_need_desc: Numbers from a routine checkup or blood test (resting blood pressure, cholesterol, glucose). You can also test with preloaded synthetic examples without personal data.
hero.disclaimer: Educational tool for health awareness. Results represent statistical model estimates, not an individual clinical diagnosis.

heart.aorta_desc: The aorta carries oxygen-rich blood from the heart to the body. CardioScan does not directly image or measure the aorta.
heart.coronary_desc: Coronary arteries supply blood to the heart muscle. Some clinical measurements can provide indirect information relevant to coronary artery disease, but this illustration does not show an individual's arteries.
heart.muscle_desc: The myocardium is the heart's muscular wall. CardioScan uses measurements from a dataset to estimate a pattern; it does not directly measure the condition of your heart muscle.
heart.overview: Your heart relies on a network of blood vessels to deliver oxygen. CardioScan explores how measurements such as blood pressure, cholesterol and exercise-related signals relate to a model's estimate.
heart.disclaimer: Educational illustration · Not a patient-specific scan

how.title: How CardioScan works
how.subtitle: A transparent machine-learning pipeline connecting routine measurements to pattern evaluation.
how.step1_desc: Provide up to 13 routine cardiovascular measurements from laboratory panels, resting vitals, or treadmill exercise stress tests. You can also explore preloaded clinical archetypes.
how.step2_desc: Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and K-Nearest Neighbors analyze non-linear patterns concurrently. A majority-voting consensus determines whether statistical indicators lean elevated or baseline.
how.step3_title: Inspect feature contributions and simulate changes
how.step3_desc: Review mathematical feature attribution rankings to see which signals influenced the calculation most. Use What-If simulation sliders to observe how shifting numbers modifies estimated risk.

combine.title: Why measurements work together
combine.subtitle: In cardiovascular health, individual numbers rarely tell the complete story. Adjust the three controls below to observe how multiple signals compound in predictive modeling.
combine.card_subtitle: Click any level to observe how simulated multi-parameter interactions compound
combine.lever1_desc: Physical outward force against artery walls. Higher pressure causes mechanical wear over time.
combine.lever2_desc: Circulating lipid particles. Excess particles can collect in arterial walls where wear occurs.
combine.lever3_desc: Waveform sag on ECG during exertion. Indicates whether heart muscle receives enough oxygen under stress.
combine.edu_note: Educational note: In real patients, individual genetics, vascular anatomy, and clinical history determine cardiac health. Machine learning models evaluate mathematical correlations within training records, not individual patient biology.
combine.story_all_normal_body: Arterial walls experience low mechanical shear stress, circulating blood lipids remain within desirable clearance ranges, and electrocardiogram waveforms show adequate myocardial oxygen perfusion. In this scenario, the algorithm assigns a low statistical likelihood of coronary artery disease.
combine.story_all_high_headline: High Mechanical Shear + Lipid Accumulation + Ischemia
combine.story_all_high_body: Elevated blood pressure creates microscopic endothelial lesions in arterial walls. High circulating cholesterol particles infiltrate these lesions to form inflammatory atherosclerotic plaques. When physical exertion increases myocardial oxygen demand, narrowed arteries cannot supply enough blood, producing ST-segment depression. When all three signals compound, the model's estimated risk surges.
combine.story_isolated_headline: Isolated Signal Elevation with Partial Compensation
combine.story_isolated_body: One primary marker is markedly elevated, placing sustained strain on either the vascular tree, metabolic clearance, or cardiac reserve. However, other compensatory indicators remain normal. Clinical algorithms weigh both the elevated signal and the protective factors to assign an intermediate risk profile.
combine.story_borderline_headline: Borderline Interplay of Multiple Mild Indicators
combine.story_borderline_body: Multiple signals are slightly outside optimal reference ranges without crossing into severe pathology. Machine learning classifiers evaluate whether subtle borderline shifts compound toward clinical significance. This demonstrates why comprehensive multi-parameter screening is clinically valuable.

scope.title: What machine learning can and cannot do
scope.subtitle: Machine learning is an effective pattern-recognition tool, but it operates with clear boundaries. Understanding what the model can and cannot tell you is essential for safe, informed health exploration.
scope.can_1_text: Evaluates non-linear relationships across all 13 indicators simultaneously, which is difficult to synthesize by mental math alone.
scope.can_2_text: Calculates feature attribution showing which variables moved the algorithm's calculation most for a specific profile.
scope.can_3_text: Allows you to simulate how hypothetical changes (such as lowering blood pressure or cholesterol) shift model predictions.
scope.can_4_text: Lets you contrast how linear models, decision tree ensembles, instance-based clusters, and support vector machines interpret the same inputs.
scope.cannot_1_text: A statistical correlation in historical data does not equal an individualized medical diagnosis. Only a qualified physician can evaluate your clinical condition.
scope.cannot_2_text: The 13 variables represent a specific subset of cardiovascular markers, not a complete diagnostic workup such as direct catheterization or coronary angiography.
scope.cannot_3_text: Models estimate baseline statistical patterns from historical data, not the imminent timing, plaque rupture risk, or acute likelihood of a heart attack.
scope.cannot_4_text: CardioScan is strictly an educational tool. Never alter, discontinue, or initiate medications based on algorithmic estimates.

research.title: Research and methodology
research.subtitle: CardioScan is trained on open historical clinical research data. Here is how the models, training pipeline, and attribution calculations are constructed.
research.card1_desc: CardioScan uses the 13-feature heart disease dataset originating from the 1988 Cleveland Clinic Foundation study in the UCI Machine Learning Repository. The source file contains 1,025 total records, which resolves to 302 unique records after exact duplicate removal. The target variable denotes angiographic coronary artery disease (≥ 50% diameter narrowing in one or more major coronary vessels).
research.card2_desc: Predictions are computed using four supervised learning algorithms: Logistic Regression (L2 regularization baseline), Random Forest (100 decision trees), K-Nearest Neighbors (k=5, Euclidean metric), and Support Vector Machine (RBF kernel with Platt probability estimation). The consensus risk tier uses majority voting across Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and KNN, while SVM is available as an independent selectable model.
research.card3_desc: Feature attributions are calculated via sampling-based marginal probability shifts against background reference distributions. A fixed random seed (seed 42) ensures identical explanation values for identical inputs. These attribution scores describe mathematical algorithm weighting within the model, not biological cause and effect.
research.card4_desc: Model accuracy depends strictly on the dataset and evaluation protocol. Because the training data reflects a specific hospital referral cohort from 1988 with 302 unique records, evaluated test scores cannot be assumed to generalize to modern, diverse clinical patient populations. CardioScan is an educational exploration tool and is not clinically deployable or diagnostically validated.
research.spec1_desc: Continuous features (age, trestbps, chol, thalach, oldpeak) are standardized using StandardScaler fitted on the training split to prevent data leakage. Categorical predictors (cp, restecg, slope, thal) are numerically encoded adhering to original Cleveland Clinic protocols. Missing values in ca and thal are handled via median imputation.
research.spec2_desc: The consensus ensemble evaluates the predictions of Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and KNN concurrently. If two or more models predict elevated risk (> 0.50 probability threshold), the consensus flag is assigned as positive. Standalone SVM operates with Platt scaling (probability=True) to output continuous probability estimates.
research.spec3_desc: The inference pipeline executes the complete 3-model ensemble and 13 feature attributions in milliseconds on standard hardware, enabling fluid updates in the What-If simulation workspace.

cta.title: Understand what your numbers may be saying

cta.privacy_text: Assessments can be performed without providing your name, contact details, or personal identity. If you create an account to save history, your email is stored securely solely for authentication.
cta.notice_text: CardioScan provides educational model estimates and does not diagnose disease or prescribe treatment. Always discuss clinical tests with a licensed healthcare provider.

It is not an FDA-cleared diagnostic device and cannot substitute for professional medical advice, clinical diagnosis, or individualized treatment plans from a licensed healthcare provider. If you suspect you are experiencing symptoms of a heart attack or cardiovascular emergency, contact emergency services immediately.

methodology.title: Evaluation Methodology, Dataset Integrity & Clinical Limitations
methodology.subtitle: Scientific transparency regarding training data, duplicate records, and clinical boundaries
methodology.card1_desc: Models were evaluated using 13 physiological parameters from the UCI Cleveland Clinic Foundation heart disease cohort (hemodynamics, metabolic panels, and stress ECG). Target prevalence in unique patients is 54.3% positive and 45.7% negative.
methodology.card2_title: The Duplicate Record Finding & Data Leakage
methodology.card2_desc: A critical dataset audit identified that the raw 1,025-row heart.csv dataset contains 723 duplicate copies of only 302 unique patients. When partitioned without deduplication, 97.1% of test rows are exact copies of training rows, artificially inflating Random Forest test accuracy to 98.5%. When evaluated with leakage-safe 5-fold cross-validation on unique patients, true generalization is ~82.5% across all models.
methodology.card3_desc: High statistical benchmark scores (ROC-AUC ~0.90) do not guarantee individualized accuracy or clinical safety. Retrospective academic datasets lack contemporary ethnic, demographic, and comorbidity diversity. CardioScan is not cleared by regulatory authorities and must not replace professional clinical judgment.

glossary.title: Healthcare Machine Learning Metric Glossary
glossary.subtitle: Understanding evaluation terminology in cardiovascular risk estimation
glossary.sens_body: The proportion of heart disease cases in the cohort correctly identified as positive. In screening evaluation, higher sensitivity prioritizes cases for secondary clinical review.
glossary.spec_body: The proportion of non-disease individuals correctly classified as negative. In screening evaluation, higher specificity reduces false alarms on healthy individuals, helping limit avoidable secondary testing.
glossary.ppv_body: Out of all patients flagged by the model, the percentage who actually have cardiovascular disease. PPV depends heavily on disease prevalence in the tested population.
glossary.auc_body: A threshold-independent measure of discrimination: the probability that the algorithm will assign a higher risk score to a randomly chosen disease patient than to a healthy individual.
